name: Verify contact lists with Zelnum using HTTP Request and Wait

parameters.content:
# Verify contact lists with Zelnum using HTTP Request and Wait

## Who is this for?

For operations teams and developers preparing contact lists for a CRM import. Verify phone numbers or email addresses in bulk with Zelnum using n8n's built-in HTTP Request and Wait nodes.

## What it does

Normalizes and deduplicates your list, checks the current product minimum, and requests a non-billable quote. Submission requires explicit billing approval and a USDT spending limit. Bounded polling distinguishes failed or expired results from pending work. Completed ZIP/CSV results download as n8n binary data. Resume an existing task without another paid submission.

## How to set up

1. [Register with Zelnum](https://app.zelnum.com), create an API key in API Center, and fund your account for paid checks.
2. Create Header Auth with name `X-API-Key` and your private key; select it on all five authenticated HTTP Request nodes.
3. Configure the series, product slug, list, and request key. Keep `execute_billable=false` to preview pricing; set a spending limit before enabling submission.
4. Save the returned task ID. Use `resume_task_id` to continue status checks or downloads later.

## Requirements and customization

Requires compatible built-in n8n nodes. Meet the selected product's minimum; this quoted-array template accepts up to 10,000 input contacts. Attach storage after the validated download; no file writer is included.

See the [Zelnum API documentation](https://docs.zelnum.com) for product coverage and result retention, or visit [Zelnum](https://zelnum.com). Product verdicts do not establish contact consent.

nodes.name: Step 1 — configure a batch or resume

parameters.content:
## 1. Configure your own list
The Edit Fields node accepts comma/newline-separated contacts (one series per batch). Normalization and optional deduplication report removed duplicates. Select a current async product slug; do not guess its minimum. This quoted-array flow supports 10,000 input rows.

**Resume:** set only `resume_task_id` and polling settings to inspect an existing task without quoting or submitting again.

nodes.name: Step 2 — current minimum and safe quote

parameters.content:
## 2. Check the minimum and quote
The catalog supplies the current product-specific minimum; validation applies it after optional deduplication. Do not pad lists with dummy contacts. Phone country is required; email omits it.

`execute_billable=false` ends at a price preview. A paid run requests a fresh quote and must fit `max_total_usdt`.

## 3. Submit once, save the task ID
Paid submission sends the exact quoted body, quote headers, and your stable idempotency key. The HTTP node does not retry automatically. Keep the same inputs/key after uncertain errors. Save `task_id` before closing the run; it is your handle for recovery.

Use a separate new key for a genuinely new batch.

## 4. Bounded polling and safe download
One task is polled every 3–5 seconds, at most `max_poll_attempts` times. Network time adds to the interval; the workflow has a 30-minute execution limit. Failed tasks and completed-but-expired/unavailable results go to terminal output, not another polling cycle.

Only an exact `api.zelnum.com` result URL receives your credential; redirects are disabled. ZIP/CSV must have a successful, non-empty binary response. The final `data` binary can be downloaded in n8n or connected to your own storage node. No explicit file writer is included.

## Private credential setup
Create Header Auth: Name `X-API-Key`; Value your private Zelnum key from [API Center](https://app.zelnum.com). Select the same credential on the five authenticated HTTP nodes: quote, submit, status, metadata, download. The public catalog needs no credential.

## Recovery and privacy
A polling limit does not cancel the remote task. Save its ID and use `resume_task_id`; do not create another paid submission. Download before API `expires_at`. A 404 may mean expired, missing, or inaccessible; 422 means validation/not-ready, not expiry.

Only process contacts you have a lawful basis to use. Execution saving is disabled by default; never pin real lists or export credentials. Use a streaming client for files too large for your n8n memory.
